Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call: 

1) Stakeholders we heard on the call (please confirm/add):
   - Economic buyer: Jenna Morales, VP Product (you indicated budget owner)
   - Security: Priya Shah, CISO (you said initial reviewer)
   - Engineering: Carlos Mendes, VP Engineering (technical owner)
   - Procurement: procurement@atlashealth.com (formal contract contact)

2) Decision criteria you listed: latency under 200ms for core API calls, SOC2 compliance, predictable unit economics, and gradual rollout to prod.

3) Systems in scope (please confirm):
   - Atlas public API (prod) — user-facing inference calls
   - Internal data pipeline (batch jobs that feed embeddings)
   - A/B test environment (staging) for Canary rollout

4) Security kickoff items we can start immediately:
   - I attached our "security intake" PDF (short questionnaire) — if you can return that to us by EOD Friday we will queue it for the security team.
   - Technical contact for questionnaire and any service-account/key provisioning: please confirm name and email.
   - If you prefer an SSP call, Rishi (cc) can run a 30-min technical scope on Wed morning.

Next steps (proposed):
 - You confirm stakeholder list and systems-in-scope (reply inline).
 - Priya or your security delegate fills the intake PDF and uploads to the Google doc link below.
 - Rishi to schedule a 30-min technical scope session once we have confirmed systems (we can record it).

Hi all — quick technical notes ahead of the Wed/Tue session: 

1) For the intake, two things we need to confirm from Atlas:
   - Which environments hold real PII (prod only or staging too?). That affects whether we request architecture diagrams and data-flow artifacts.
   - Does Atlas use a KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) for service keys? If so, which tenant/account?

2) For the patient-messaging worker: if it processes PII in batch, we will treat it as "in-scope" for encryption and logging requirements. We'll ask for a minimal list of endpoints it calls and sample logs (sanitized).

3) Evidence we can provide right away: SOC 2 summary, encryption-at-rest notes, and our key-management integration page. I'll attach the short evidence pack to the intake doc before the technical session.

If you can confirm the above two items, I can prepare a short agenda for the tech session and include a checklist for required artifacts.
